functional.summary: Redis 7.4 in-memory cache infrastructure for ETP applications. Not a JVM runtime service, REST API, or cache proxy.
provides: Redis 7.4 server (Docker image redis:7.4-alpine in local development)
Redis wire protocol connectivity for consumer applications via Redis client libraries
Configuration and operational conventions for environment-resolved endpoints and secrets
doesNotProvide: ETP REST APIs for cache access or Redis administration
Application cache keys, TTL policies, or invalidation logic (consumer-owned)
Cache-aside orchestration or automatic cache wiring (future platform scope)
Connection brokering or cache proxy in the ETP runtime path
applicationResponsibilities: What data is cached and cache-aside behavior (HIT/MISS → backing store such as PostgreSQL)
Cache key design and namespace conventions
Redis client library integration (e.g. Spring Data Redis / Lettuce)
infrastructureResponsibilities: Persistence policy for the deployment environment (optional in dev)

clients: Jedis and other Redis-compatible Java clients
redis.logicalDatabase: Redis logical database index 0–15 (default 0); key-prefix isolation recommended for multi-tenant or multi-app sharing
redis.integration: Applications configure spring.data.redis.* (or equivalent) and connect directly — no ETP Redis middleware

documentation.note: Infrastructure capability — no OpenAPI service surface

credentials: Redis password (requirepass / ACL user password) supplied via environment variables or secret manager
Never store live credentials in the Capability Registry contract document or registration payload
secretReferences: Production: secret manager / platform secret injection (deployment-specific)

authentication.acls: Redis ACLs supported by Redis 7; not configured in repository defaults — deployment responsibility for non-dev

networkAccess: Local development: Redis port published via Docker Compose (default host port 56379)
Non-dev: restrict Redis port to application network; not configured in repository defaults
applicationIsolation: Recommended: per-application key prefix or namespace (e.g. uam:, iam:)
Optional: separate logical database index per application on shared Redis
Strong isolation: dedicated Redis instance or cluster per environment/application (deployment-specific)

tlsSsl.detail: Local compose uses plain TCP. TLS is a deployment responsibility for managed Redis (ElastiCache, Azure Cache for Redis) in non-dev environments.

limitations: Single shared Redis password in local compose example
No TLS in local Docker defaults
No Redis ACL users defined in repository compose — password-only auth for v1.0.0 local dev
futureHardening: Redis ACL users with least-privilege per application
Private network-only endpoints with no public port exposure

deployment.versionRationale: Redis 7.4 is the current stable Redis 7 line with wide Docker availability and compatibility with Spring Data Redis / Lettuce. No prior Redis version existed in the ETP repository.
deployment.implementationModel: Infrastructure container — not an ETP Spring Boot artifact

localDockerReference.persistence: Named volume etp-redis-data (default Redis RDB snapshots to /data)

environmentSpecific: Docker Compose (local development — implemented in capabilities/redis/)
Kubernetes Redis operator or Helm chart (deployment-specific — not defined in repository)
AWS ElastiCache for Redis (deployment target — not implemented in repository)
Azure Cache for Redis (deployment target — not implemented in repository)
deployment.endpoint: Host and port from deployment environment

nfr.connectionReliability: Consumer applications should treat Redis as optional for cache-aside (degrade to backing store on failure) or require connectivity before readiness — consumer policy
nfr.healthReadiness: Container health via redis-cli PING (local compose); consumer readiness via Redis connectivity check in application Actuator health contributor
nfr.connectionPool: Lettuce connection pooling via Spring Boot defaults when using spring-boot-starter-data-redis; tunable via spring.data.redis.lettuce.pool.*
operationalRequirements: Start Redis before consumers that require cache connectivity at startup
No numeric latency or availability SLOs defined in repository for v1.0.0

startup: Start consumer application with Redis client configuration
readiness: Redis: redis-cli PING healthcheck in local Docker Compose
Consumers: application-level Redis health contributor (e.g. Spring Boot Actuator redis health when configured)
operations.connectivity: Verified by consumer Redis client, not by a dedicated ETP Redis service

persistence.localDevelopment: Named Docker volume with default Redis persistence; acceptable for dev cache warm-up
persistence.productionGuidance: Deployment-specific — ElastiCache/Azure policies or explicit no-persistence for pure cache tiers

operations.environmentConfiguration: Per-service environment variables (ETP_REDIS_*) — see configuration section

clientConsumers: Spring Boot services with spring-boot-starter-data-redis and Lettuce
Any Redis-compatible client targeting Redis 7 wire protocol
expectations: Consumers use Redis commands supported by Redis 7
Cache-aside pattern: application handles HIT/MISS and backing store (e.g. PostgreSQL) — not ETP Redis capability
notIncludedInV1_0_0: Redis Cluster or Sentinel automation in repository

applicationDefinition.description: Composition-time selection of etp.redis capability version; required vs optional; logical usage intent (cache tier) — no plaintext secrets
examples: capability: etp.redis, version: 1.0.0, required: false for cache-aside with PostgreSQL fallback

environmentConfiguration.description: Deployment-time resolution of host, port, TLS, secret references — application does not hardcode Docker vs ElastiCache vs Azure

applicationImplementation.description: Runtime Spring Boot or client configuration injected from environment

parameters.name: TLS
parameters.description: spring.data.redis.ssl.enabled when deployment provides TLS endpoint

parameters.name: key prefix / namespace
parameters.description: Consumer-defined cache key convention — not ETP capability configuration

dependencies.note: Redis is infrastructure. Registry dependencies[] is empty. Consumers connect via Redis client directly. Backing stores (e.g. etp.postgresql) are separate consumer dependencies, not registry dependencies of etp.redis.
